contracts.commit_point: The middleware's pre-execution interrupt on each record_movement tool call: the graph pauses with paused state persisted by the checkpointer ('an interrupt has to persist the paused state somewhere or there is nothing to resume into', graph.py:134-136) and the tool must not execute until the CLI resumes it with the human decision (cli.py:95-104); if execution proceeds, the write commits through the POST /movements request in InventoryClient.record_movement (client.py:205-210), the terminal supplied code point of the movement write.
contracts.declared_mechanism: HumanInTheLoopMiddleware constructed in build_middleware with a per-tool InterruptOnConfig(allowed_decisions=['approve','edit','reject'], description=_describe_write) for every name in GUARDED_TOOLS={'record_movement'}, attached via create_agent(model, tools, middleware=build_middleware(require_approval), checkpointer=InMemorySaver()); the CLI detects '__interrupt__' in the astream and resumes with Command(resume=_ask_human(...)), where _ask_human is the operator approval gate returning one decision per action request.
contracts.forbidden_condition: The record_movement tool call executing (and thereby committing the inventory movement write) without a human approve/edit/reject decision resolving the middleware interrupt — i.e., the world-changing write running unattended through agent tool dispatch.
pending_binding_information: The MCP-server tool implementation for record_movement (which would bind the guarded agent tool to InventoryClient.record_movement and the POST /movements write) is not in the supplied sources; the linkage rests on the tool name in GUARDED_TOOLS matching InventoryClient.record_movement and the client docstring 'The HTTP client the MCP tools call' (client.py:1-7).
The downstream persistence path for POST /movements (REST facade -> database) and the 'publishes a domain event' behavior described in _describe_write (graph.py:67) are not in supplied source.
Framework semantics of langchain HumanInTheLoopMiddleware/InterruptOnConfig (exact pause/resume guarantees) are not supplied; only their registration and the CLI resume wiring are evidenced.
contracts.protected_operation: Pre-execution interception and human resolution of the agent's record_movement tool call, whose execution the source describes as 'WRITE to the inventory database ... records a real stock movement and publishes a domain event' and as a write that should occur only when clearly asked for.
contracts.protected_resource: The 'record_movement' MCP tool listed in GUARDED_TOOLS — the guarded write path to the inventory platform, materialized in supplied code as the POST /movements request in InventoryClient.record_movement.
contracts.protection_obligation: Any agent-invoked execution of the 'record_movement' tool (the guarded write to the inventory database issued via POST /movements) must first be interrupted by HumanInTheLoopMiddleware and resolved by a human approve/edit/reject decision before the tool executes. This merges the approval clauses of both reviewers' first- and second-phase wording.
scope_limits: Gating applies only when require_approval is True: build_middleware skips HumanInTheLoopMiddleware otherwise (graph.py:89-107), build_agent defaults require_approval=True (graph.py:122), and the CLI run() path uses that default (cli.py:88).
Only tools named in GUARDED_TOOLS={'record_movement'} are gated; reads run unattended by design (graph.py:32-33).
InterruptOnConfig allows approve/edit/reject (graph.py:98-100), but the supplied CLI resolver emits only approve or reject; no edit path is implemented in _ask_human (cli.py:76-83).
Interrupt persistence uses InMemorySaver, i.e., in-memory per-process checkpoint state (graph.py:28, 134-136).

The claim that record_movement is the sole write path is supported by the supplied views ('# The write', client.py:181-183) but the unit scope states repository enumeration is not complete, so exclusivity cannot be verified.
ToolCallLimitMiddleware (run_limit=15, exit_behavior='continue', graph.py:36-40, 91-93) is a gateway rate-budget control and is not part of this approval obligation.

contracts.commit_point: Emission of the POST /movements request with the Idempotency-Key header (client.py:205-210) — the last supplied code point before persistence at which duplicate attempts become collapsible ('replayed: true ... the stock moves once', client.py:52-53).
contracts.declared_mechanism: movement_idempotency_key(session_id, sku, warehouse_code, movement_type, quantity) deriving a deterministic uuid5 key seeded from the intent under the fixed IDEMPOTENCY_NAMESPACE, sent as the 'Idempotency-Key' header on the POST in InventoryClient.record_movement.
contracts.forbidden_condition: A duplicate movement write that is not collapsed: a write issued without the derived stable key (e.g., a random per-attempt key), such that 'every retry [is] a NEW movement and silently double-count[s] stock', or the model calling the same write twice for the same physical event.
pending_binding_information: The code that calls movement_idempotency_key and passes the key into InventoryClient.record_movement (presumably the MCP server's record_movement tool, deriving session_id from agent tool-call context) is not in supplied source, so the agent-generated-input dataflow into this guard is not established.
Whether any non-agent code path issues the same POST /movements write without this mechanism cannot be determined from the supplied views.
contracts.protected_operation: The write performed by InventoryClient.record_movement: the POST {rest_root}/movements request, labeled '# The write' in the client.
contracts.protected_resource: The inventory movements resource (stock records in the inventory database) reached via settings.rest_root + '/movements' through the gateway.
contracts.protection_obligation: The inventory movement write (the POST /movements request issued by InventoryClient.record_movement) must carry an intent-derived Idempotency-Key so that repeated attempts at the same logical movement within a session collapse into one recorded movement instead of double-counting stock. This merges the idempotency clauses of both reviewers' wording.
scope_limits: The key seed covers session_id, sku, warehouse_code, movement_type and quantity only (client.py:58); reference_type and notes are excluded from the seed.
session_id is deliberately in the hash so recording the same movement in a later session is treated as a legitimate business event, not a retry (client.py:55-56).
Collapse depends on the server honoring Idempotency-Key replay semantics ('replayed: true'); that behavior is asserted only in the client docstring and no server-side code is supplied.
Cross-process key stability depends on the fixed IDEMPOTENCY_NAMESPACE, whose value is redacted in the supplied source (client.py:20-22).
Settings values (rest_root, timeout_seconds, api_key_header, api_key) come from inventory_mcp.config, which is not supplied.
